review_notes: I read the whole target file and the defining file IndependentRadiusProjections.lean. That file has only the `radiusPairProjection_apply_zero` and `radiusPairProjection_apply_one` simp lemmas. It has no equality/ext characterisation for `radiusPairProjection` and no apply lemmas for `radiusTripleProjection`. I grepped for other uses of the same PiLp ext pattern; it appears three times in the radius-projection files (lines 30 and 47 of the definition file, line 53 of the target). I did not run Lean, so the suggested lemma and its simp behaviour are untested. I found no loops or competing simp rules; the problem is a missing canonical lemma.

findings.excerpt:
have hpairEq (a : α) (i j : ι) (hij : i ≠ j) (x : Plane) :
      f (a,⟨(i,j),hij⟩) x = p (a,⟨(i,j),hij⟩) r ↔
        ρ a i x = r i ∧ ρ a j x = r j := by
findings.problem: The proof needs the fact that two values of `radiusPairProjection i j` are equal exactly when their i and j coordinates agree. The defining file has no simp or ext lemma for this. It only has `radiusPairProjection_apply_zero` and `radiusPairProjection_apply_one`, which evaluate at 0 and 1 but cannot decide equality of two Plane points. So the proof rebuilds the fact by hand inside a local `have`. It applies `PiLp.continuousLinearEquiv ... .injective`, then `funext` and `fin_cases`. The same unfolding is repeated at lines 30 and 47 of IndependentRadiusProjections.lean. The local statement is also stated for the `f`/`p` lets rather than the projection itself, so no other file can reuse it.
findings.proposed_change: In IndependentRadiusProjections.lean, add a lemma such as `radiusPairProjection_eq_iff (i j) (t s : ι → ℝ) : radiusPairProjection i j t = radiusPairProjection i j s ↔ t i = s i ∧ t j = s j`. Mark it `@[simp]`. Its left side is a head-symbol equation and its right side is strictly simpler, so it cannot loop. It can reuse the existing `_apply_zero` and `_apply_one` lemmas for the forward direction. The proof of `hpairEq` then reduces to `simp [f, p, radiusPairProjection_eq_iff]`, or to a direct `.mpr`/`.mp` call.
findings.benefit: The projection-equality normal form `t i = s i ∧ t j = s j` becomes available to every later user of these projections, including the surjectivity proofs and the GenericSurfaceLevels/GenericCircularRadii consumers. It removes the repeated PiLp/fin_cases boilerplate.

@[simp] lemma radiusPairProjection_apply_zero (i j : ι) (t : ι → ℝ) :

findings.problem: `radiusTripleProjection` is a plain `def` built with `.prod`. It has no simp lemmas, neither for the Prod components nor for equality. To prove equality of two triple-projection values, the proof applies `Prod.ext`, reuses the local pair lemma, and relies on `he.2.2` being definitionally `(proj k) _ = ...`. In the definition file, `radiusTripleProjection_surjective` has to use `change radiusPairProjection i j _ = y.1` and `simp [radiusTripleProjection]`. The triple projection therefore has no canonical simp normal form, and users must unfold it or rely on defeq.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp]` lemmas next to the definition. These are `radiusTripleProjection_apply_fst : (radiusTripleProjection i j k t).1 = radiusPairProjection i j t` and `radiusTripleProjection_apply_snd : (radiusTripleProjection i j k t).2 = t k`. Also add an `radiusTripleProjection_eq_iff` stating `t i = s i ∧ t j = s j ∧ t k = s k`, built from the pair lemma and `Prod.ext_iff`. The final bullet then becomes `(radiusTripleProjection_eq_iff ..).mpr ⟨..⟩`. Alternatively, `simp [g, q, radiusTripleProjection]` closes it without relying on defeq.
findings.benefit: The triple projection gets a canonical simp normal form, and its use stops depending on definitional unfolding through `Prod.ext`. It would also fix the ad-hoc `change` in `radiusTripleProjection_surjective`.
